name: Roland RE-201 Space Echo
originalPurpose: A tape echo and spring reverb in one box, sold to guitarists and studios on being quieter and far more reliable than the tape delays before it.
whatActuallyHappened: A loop of tape runs past three playback heads, and the controls that set the delay time and the feedback are built to be turned while sound is passing through them. That turns a setting into a gesture. In Kingston and later in London, a word or a single snare hit gets pushed into the feedback until the repeats pile up and swallow themselves, then pulled back. The runaway howl on a dub record is not a preset. It is somebody's hand.
priceStory: One box doing what a tape machine, an operator and a live room would otherwise have to do between them, and rugged enough to survive a studio with no air conditioning. That combination, rather than any particular price, is why it spread so far beyond the guitarists it was aimed at.
hook: An echo unit built to be reliable, used instead as something to play with one hand while the record runs.

blurb.age7: A box that repeats a sound over and over, and you can make the repeats pile up until they take over everything.
blurb.age13: Inside is a loop of tape and three heads that read it, so a sound comes back at you several times. The trick is that you can turn the knobs while music is going through it. Turn the feedback up far enough and the repeats feed themselves and build into a roar. Dub producers used that as a thing you do at a moment, not a setting you choose beforehand.
blurb.adult: The RE-201 matters here because its controls are performable and its failure mode is musical. Self-oscillation at high feedback, plus the pitch instability of a tape loop under load, produce the smearing and the runaway bloom that dub's vocabulary is built from. Roland engineered for stability and shipped an instrument.
